source.text: מַשְׂכִּ֗יל לְאָ֫סָ֥ףהַאֲזִ֣ינָה עַ֭מִּי תּוֹרָתִ֑י הַטּ֥וּ אָ֝זְנְכֶ֗ם לְאִמְרֵי־פִֽי׃

records.literal_gloss: A maskil of Asaph. Give ear, my people, [to] my instruction; incline your ear to [the] words of my mouth.

en.L: A maskil of Asaph. \q Give ear, my people, [to] my instruction; \q incline your ear to the words of my mouth.
en.B: A maskil of Asaph. \q My people, listen closely to my instruction; \q bend your ears to what I say.
en.R: A song to teach, by Asaph. \q My people, listen to what I teach you. \q Pay attention to what I say.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: maskil: probably a skillful or instructive song
decisions.reason: As in 32:1, the word (maskil) comes from a verb meaning to be wise or to give insight. Its exact sense as a kind of song is no longer known; this psalm is plainly meant to teach.

decisions.choice: Asaph: a leader of the temple singers
decisions.reason: Asaph was a Levite whom David appointed to lead the singing before the ark (1 Chronicles 16:5-7); his family carried on the work (1 Chronicles 25:1-2). Psalms 50 and 73-83 bear his name.

decisions.choice: listen, my people: a teacher's call
decisions.reason: The psalm opens like a teacher of wisdom calling his pupils (Proverbs 4:1-2) and like the song of Moses (Deuteronomy 32:1). It is the longest retelling of Israel's history in the Psalms, from Egypt to David, told as a warning.

decisions.choice: instruction: teaching
decisions.reason: The word (torah) here is the psalmist's own teaching, as in Proverbs 3:1. Literal and Balanced say "instruction", Readable "teach".

decisions.choice: A song to teach; listen
decisions.reason: As in 32:1, Readable gives the likely sense of the term (m2).

source.text: אֶפְתְּחָ֣ה בְמָשָׁ֣ל פִּ֑י אַבִּ֥יעָה חִ֝יד֗וֹת מִנִּי־קֶֽדֶם׃

records.literal_gloss: I will open in a parable my mouth; I will pour forth riddles from antiquity,

en.L: I will open my mouth in a parable; \q I will pour forth riddles from of old,
en.B: I will open my mouth to speak a parable; \q I will bring out the hidden lessons of long ago,
en.R: I will teach you by telling a story. \q I will explain the puzzles of the past.

decisions.choice: a parable: a lesson drawn from a comparison
decisions.reason: The word (mashal) covers proverbs, sayings and lessons that set one thing beside another. Here Israel's history is told so that its lesson can be seen (49:5).

decisions.choice: riddles: sayings whose meaning must be drawn out
decisions.reason: The word (chidot) means riddles or puzzling sayings (Judges 14:12; Proverbs 1:6). The old story holds a meaning not seen at first glance.

decisions.choice: quoted in Matthew 13:35
decisions.reason: Matthew quotes this verse to explain why Jesus taught the crowds in parables, saying that his teaching fulfilled what was spoken by the prophet, and that he spoke of things hidden since the world began (Matthew 13:34-35).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The "riddles" are described in verse 3 ("which we have heard"), so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: telling a story; the puzzles of the past
decisions.reason: Readable uses plain words for the two kinds of saying (m1, m2).

source.text: אֲשֶׁ֣ר שָׁ֭מַעְנוּ וַנֵּדָעֵ֑ם וַ֝אֲבוֹתֵ֗ינוּ סִפְּרוּ־לָֽנוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: which we have heard and known them, and our fathers have recounted to us.

en.L: which we have heard and known, \q and our fathers have recounted to us.
en.B: what we have heard and learned, \q what our forebears passed on to us.
en.R: We have heard these things and know them well. \q Our parents and grandparents told them to us.

decisions.choice: our fathers: our ancestors
decisions.reason: The word ('avot) means fathers, and in the plural the earlier generations of the people. The psalm will call them the stubborn generation of the wilderness (verse 8).

decisions.choice: our forebears (B); our parents and grandparents (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable use words that take in the whole earlier generation (m1); Literal keeps "fathers".

source.text: לֹ֤א נְכַחֵ֨ד׀מִבְּנֵיהֶ֗ם לְד֥וֹר אַחֲר֗וֹן מְֽ֭סַפְּרִים תְּהִלּ֣וֹת יְהוָ֑ה וֶעֱזוּז֥וֹ וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר עָשָֽׂה׃

records.literal_gloss: Not we will hide [them] from their children, recounting to a generation later [the] praises of YHWH, and his might, and his wonders which he has done.

en.L: We will not hide [them] from their children, \q recounting to a later generation the praises of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} might, and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.
en.B: We will not conceal them from their children; \q we will pass on to those who come after us the deeds for which {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} is praised, \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength, and the marvels {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has worked.
en.R: We will not keep these things from the children. \q We will tell the next generation the great things {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has done. \q We will tell them how strong {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is and what amazing things {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done.

decisions.choice: the praises of the LORD: deeds worthy of praise
decisions.reason: The word (tehillot) means praises, and here the acts for which God is praised, as the parallel "his might and his wonders" shows (9:15).

decisions.choice: their children: the descendants of our ancestors
decisions.reason: "Their" refers to the fathers of verse 3. Their children are the speaker's own people and the generations still to come.

decisions.choice: telling the next generation: as the law commands
decisions.reason: Israel was told to teach its children what God had done in Egypt (Exodus 13:8, 14; Deuteronomy 6:20-25). The psalm itself is that teaching.

source.text: וַיָּ֤קֶם עֵד֨וּת׀בְּֽיַעֲקֹ֗ב וְתוֹרָה֮ שָׂ֤ם בְּיִשְׂרָ֫אֵ֥ל אֲשֶׁ֣ר צִ֭וָּה אֶת־אֲבוֹתֵ֑ינוּ לְ֝הוֹדִיעָ֗ם לִבְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he established a testimony in Jacob, and an instruction he set in Israel, which he commanded our fathers to make them known to their children,

en.L: He established a testimony in Jacob, and set instruction in Israel, \q which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded our fathers \q to make known to their children,
en.B: He laid down a solemn charge in Jacob and set up instruction in Israel; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ordered our forebears \q to teach these to their children,
en.R: God gave rules and teaching to Israel, the family of Jacob. \q He told our ancestors to teach them to their children.

decisions.choice: a testimony: God's solemn charge to his people
decisions.reason: The word ('edut) is God's witness to his will, the terms of the covenant written on the tablets (Exodus 25:16; 19:8 in the Psalms). With instruction (torah) it means all God taught Israel at Sinai.

decisions.choice: teach them to their children: Deuteronomy's command
decisions.reason: Moses commands Israel to teach God's words to their children (Deuteronomy 4:9-10; 6:7; 11:19).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The purpose of the command follows in verses 6-8, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: God; the family of Jacob
decisions.reason: Readable names who acts (verse 4 names the LORD) and says who "Jacob" is.

source.text: לְמַ֤עַן יֵדְע֨וּ׀דּ֣וֹר אַ֭חֲרוֹן בָּנִ֣ים יִוָּלֵ֑דוּ יָ֝קֻ֗מוּ וִֽיסַפְּר֥וּ לִבְנֵיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: so that may know a generation later, children [who] will be born; they will arise and recount [them] to their children,

en.L: so that a later generation might know, children [yet] to be born, \q [who] would arise and recount [them] to their children,
en.B: so that those born later, children not yet born, would know them, \q and would grow up and tell them to their own children,
en.R: Then the people born later would know them too. \q When those children grew up, they would tell their own children.

decisions.choice: arise and recount: each generation passes it on
decisions.reason: The chain runs from the fathers to their children, to children not yet born, and on to their children: four generations in verses 5-6.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verses 7-8, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: וְיָשִׂ֥ימוּ בֵֽאלֹהִ֗ים כִּ֫סְלָ֥ם וְלֹ֣א יִ֭שְׁכְּחוּ מַֽעַלְלֵי־אֵ֑ל וּמִצְוֺתָ֥יו יִנְצֹֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: and they will set in God their confidence, and not forget [the] deeds of God, and his commandments they will keep,

en.L: and they would set their confidence in God, \q and not forget the deeds of God, \q but keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commandments,
en.B: so that they would rest their hope on God, \q remember the works of God, \q and keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands,
en.R: So they would trust in God \q and remember what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} has done. \q They would obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} commands.

decisions.choice: confidence: what one leans on
decisions.reason: The word (kesel) means confidence or hope, the thing one relies on (Job 31:24).

decisions.choice: remembering leads to obeying
decisions.reason: Forgetting what God has done is the root of disobedience in this psalm (verses 11, 42); remembering it leads to trust and obedience.

source.text: וְלֹ֤א יִהְי֨וּ׀כַּאֲבוֹתָ֗ם דּוֹר֮ סוֹרֵ֪ר וּמֹ֫רֶ֥ה דּ֭וֹר לֹא־הֵכִ֣ין לִבּ֑וֹ וְלֹא־נֶאֶמְנָ֖ה אֶת־אֵ֣ל רוּחֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: and not they will be like their fathers, a generation stubborn and rebellious, a generation [that] did not make firm its heart, and not was faithful with God its spirit.

en.L: and not be like their fathers, a stubborn and rebellious generation, \q a generation that did not set its heart firm, \q and whose spirit was not faithful to God.
en.B: and would not be like their ancestors, a defiant and rebellious generation, \q whose hearts were never steady \q and whose spirits did not stay true to God.
en.R: They would not be like their ancestors, who were stubborn and turned against God. \q Those people did not stay loyal to God, and they could not be trusted.

decisions.choice: stubborn and rebellious: the language of Deuteronomy
decisions.reason: The pair is used of a son who will not obey (Deuteronomy 21:18), and the song of Moses calls the wilderness generation crooked and without faithfulness (Deuteronomy 32:5, 20).

decisions.choice: did not make firm its heart: was never settled in loyalty
decisions.reason: To "make the heart firm" is to fix one's mind and will steadily on God (57:8; 1 Samuel 7:3). Verse 37 returns to it.

decisions.choice: stubborn and rebellious
decisions.reason: The first word (sorer) is turning aside obstinately; the second (moreh) is defying authority. The second verb returns in verses 17, 40 and 56.

source.text: בְּֽנֵי־אֶפְרַ֗יִם נוֹשְׁקֵ֥י רוֹמֵי־קָ֑שֶׁת הָ֝פְכ֗וּ בְּי֣וֹם קְרָֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Ephraim, armed ones, shooters of [the] bow, turned back on [the] day of battle.

en.L: The sons of Ephraim, armed [and] shooting with the bow, \q turned back on the day of battle.
en.B: The Ephraimites, armed and skilled with the bow, \q fled when the day of battle came.
en.R: The soldiers of Ephraim had bows and arrows, \q but they ran away when it was time to fight.

decisions.choice: Ephraim: the leading tribe of the north
decisions.reason: Ephraim, the son of Joseph, became the strongest of the northern tribes. Shiloh, where the tabernacle stood, was in its land. The psalm ends by telling how God rejected Ephraim and chose Judah, Zion and David (verses 67-72).

decisions.choice: turned back on the day of battle: which defeat is meant is not known
alternatives: a picture of Ephraim turning from God, not a battle
decisions.reason: No battle in which Ephraim's archers fled is told elsewhere. It may be the defeat at Aphek when the ark was taken from Shiloh (1 Samuel 4; verses 60-64), or the verse may picture Ephraim's faithlessness as cowardice in battle (verse 57).

decisions.choice: armed ones, shooters of the bow
decisions.reason: Two words stand side by side, "armed" and "shooters of the bow"; together they mean well-armed archers.

source.text: לֹ֣א שָׁ֭מְרוּ בְּרִ֣ית אֱלֹהִ֑ים וּ֝בְתוֹרָת֗וֹ מֵאֲנ֥וּ לָלֶֽכֶת׃

records.literal_gloss: Not they kept [the] covenant of God, and in his instruction they refused to walk.

en.L: They did not keep the covenant of God, \q and they refused to walk in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instruction.
en.B: They failed to keep the covenant God had made \q and would not follow {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} instruction.
en.R: They did not keep God's covenant. \q They would not live the way {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} teaching told them to.

decisions.choice: covenant: the bond God made with Israel
decisions.reason: The covenant (berit) is the binding agreement God made with Israel at Sinai (Exodus 24:7-8). Keeping it meant living by his instruction.

decisions.choice: walk in his instruction: live by it
decisions.reason: To walk is to live; to walk in God's instruction is to make it the path of one's life (1:1-2; 119:1).

source.text: וַיִּשְׁכְּח֥וּ עֲלִילוֹתָ֑יו וְ֝נִפְלְאוֹתָ֗יו אֲשֶׁ֣ר הֶרְאָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they forgot his deeds and his wonders which he had shown them.

en.L: And they forgot {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had shown them.
en.B: They let {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} deeds slip from memory, \q the marvels they had seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} work.
en.R: They forgot what {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had done. \q They forgot the miracles they had seen {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} do.

decisions.choice: they forgot: what Moses warned against
decisions.reason: Moses warned Israel again and again not to forget the LORD and what they had seen him do (Deuteronomy 4:9; 8:11-14). Verses 12-16 now list what was forgotten.

decisions.choice: wonders: acts beyond the ordinary
decisions.reason: The word (nifla'ot) is used of God's acts in Egypt and the wilderness (Exodus 3:20; verses 4, 12, 32).

source.text: נֶ֣גֶד אֲ֭בוֹתָם עָ֣שָׂה פֶ֑לֶא בְּאֶ֖רֶץ מִצְרַ֣יִם שְׂדֵה־צֹֽעַן׃

records.literal_gloss: Before their fathers he did wonder in [the] land of Egypt, [the] field of Zoan.

en.L: Before their fathers {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did wonders \q in the land of Egypt, the field of Zoan.
en.B: In full view of their ancestors {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} worked marvels \q in Egypt, in the region of Zoan.
en.R: While their ancestors watched, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did amazing things \q in Egypt, near the city of Zoan.

decisions.choice: the field of Zoan: the region around Zoan
decisions.reason: Zoan was an old royal city in the Nile delta (Numbers 13:22; Isaiah 19:11, 13), close to the land where Israel lived in Egypt. "Field" here means its open country.

decisions.choice: wonders in Egypt: the plagues
decisions.reason: The wonders in Egypt are the plagues (Exodus 7-12), told again in verses 43-51.

decisions.choice: near the city of Zoan
decisions.reason: Readable says what Zoan was (m1).

source.text: בָּ֣קַע יָ֭ם וַיַּֽעֲבִירֵ֑ם וַֽיַּצֶּב־מַ֥יִם כְּמוֹ־נֵֽד׃

records.literal_gloss: He split [the] sea and brought them through, and he made stand [the] waters like a heap.

en.L: He split the sea and brought them through, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made the waters stand like a heap.
en.B: He split the sea in two and took them across, \q piling up the waters in a heap.
en.R: He split the sea and led them through it. \q He made the water pile up and stand still.

decisions.choice: he split the sea: the crossing
decisions.reason: God divided the sea and Israel crossed on dry ground (Exodus 14:21-22).

decisions.choice: like a heap: as in the song at the sea
decisions.reason: The word (ned) is the one used in the song of Moses: the waters stood up "like a heap" (Exodus 15:8).

source.text: וַיַּנְחֵ֣ם בֶּעָנָ֣ן יוֹמָ֑ם וְכָל־הַ֝לַּ֗יְלָה בְּא֣וֹר אֵֽשׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he led them with the cloud by day, and all the night with [the] light of fire.

en.L: He led them with the cloud by day, \q and all the night with a light of fire.
en.B: By day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} guided them with the cloud, \q and all through the night with the glow of fire.
en.R: In the daytime {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led them with a cloud. \q All night long {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led them with a bright fire.

decisions.choice: the cloud and the fire: God's guiding presence
decisions.reason: The LORD went before Israel in a pillar of cloud by day and of fire by night (Exodus 13:21-22; Numbers 9:15-23).

source.text: יְבַקַּ֣ע צֻ֭רִים בַּמִּדְבָּ֑ר וַ֝יַּ֗שְׁקְ כִּתְהֹמ֥וֹת רַבָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: He split rocks in the wilderness, and gave drink as [the] deeps, abundant.

en.L: He split rocks in the wilderness \q and gave [them] drink as [from] the great deeps.
en.B: He broke open rocks in the desert \q and let them drink water as plentiful as the ocean depths.
en.R: In the desert {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} broke open rocks. \q He gave them plenty of water, as much as the deep sea holds.

decisions.choice: he split rocks: water from the rock
decisions.reason: God gave water from a rock at Rephidim (Exodus 17:1-7) and at Kadesh (Numbers 20:1-13). The plural "rocks" takes in both.

decisions.choice: as the deeps, abundant: a flood of water
decisions.reason: The deeps (tehomot, 77:17) are the great waters below the earth. Water poured out as if from that endless supply.

source.text: וַיּוֹצִ֣א נוֹזְלִ֣ים מִסָּ֑לַע וַיּ֖וֹרֶד כַּנְּהָר֣וֹת מָֽיִם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought out streams from [the] crag, and made flow down like rivers water.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought out streams from the crag, \q and made water flow down like rivers.
en.B: He drew streams out of the cliff \q and sent water rushing down like rivers.
en.R: He made streams of water pour out of a rock, \q and the water flowed like rivers.

decisions.choice: crag: a rock cliff
decisions.reason: Two words for rock are used: tsur (verses 15, 20), as at Rephidim (Exodus 17:6), and sela' here, as at Kadesh (Numbers 20:8, 11).

decisions.choice: streams: running water
decisions.reason: The word (nozelim) is flowing water, the same word used of the waters that stood up at the sea (Exodus 15:8).

source.text: וַיּוֹסִ֣יפוּ ע֭וֹדלַחֲטֹא־ל֑וֹ לַֽמְר֥וֹת עֶ֝לְי֗וֹן בַּצִּיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: But they went on again to sin against him, to rebel against [the] Most High in the dry land.

en.L: But they went on still to sin against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q rebelling against the Most High in the dry land.
en.B: Yet they kept on sinning against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q defying the Most High in the parched desert.
en.R: But the people kept on sinning against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q In the dry desert they turned against the God who is above all.

decisions.choice: they went on again: even after the water
decisions.reason: The verb (yasaf, "add") with "again" means they added sin to sin, though God had just given them water.

decisions.choice: rebel: defy
decisions.reason: The verb (marah) is the "rebellious" of verse 8, used again in verses 40 and 56 and of Israel at Meribah (Numbers 20:10, 24).

decisions.choice: the God who is above all
decisions.reason: As in 46:5, Readable says what the title ('Elyon) means.

source.text: וַיְנַסּוּ־אֵ֥ל בִּלְבָבָ֑ם לִֽשְׁאָל־אֹ֥כֶל לְנַפְשָֽׁם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they tested God in their heart by asking food for their soul.

en.L: And they tested God in their heart \q by asking for food for their appetite.
en.B: In their hearts they challenged God, \q insisting on food to feed their cravings.
en.R: They tried to see how far they could push God. \q They demanded the food they were hungry for.

decisions.choice: tested God: demanded that he prove himself
decisions.reason: To test God (nissah) is to challenge him to show what he can do, as Israel did at Massah, "testing" (Exodus 17:2, 7; Deuteronomy 6:16).

decisions.choice: asking food: the complaints in the wilderness
decisions.reason: The people complained that they had no bread or meat (Exodus 16:2-3) and craved the food of Egypt (Numbers 11:4-6).

decisions.choice: their soul: their appetite
decisions.reason: The word (nefesh) often means the throat and so the appetite or desire (107:9; Numbers 11:6).

decisions.choice: appetite (L); cravings (B); were hungry for (R)
decisions.reason: Here nefesh means appetite (m3), so even Literal departs from "soul", which would mislead.

source.text: וַֽיְדַבְּר֗וּ בֵּֽאלֹ֫הִ֥ים אָ֭מְרוּ הֲי֣וּכַל אֵ֑ל לַעֲרֹ֥ךְ שֻׁ֝לְחָ֗ן בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And they spoke against God; they said: Is able God to set a table in the wilderness?

en.L: And they spoke against God; \q they said, "Can God set a table in the wilderness?
en.B: They spoke against God \q and said, "Can God lay out a meal in the desert?
en.R: They complained against God. \q They said, "Can God give us a meal out here in the desert?

decisions.choice: they spoke against God: the complaint in Numbers
decisions.reason: Israel "spoke against God and against Moses" in the wilderness (Numbers 21:5), and asked who would give them meat (Numbers 11:4, 18).

decisions.choice: set a table: provide a meal
decisions.reason: To set (or "arrange") a table is to provide a full meal, as God does for the psalmist in 23:5.

decisions.choice: a quotation that runs on
decisions.reason: The people's words continue through verse 20, so the quotation opens here and closes at the end of verse 20.

source.text: הֵ֤ן הִכָּה־צ֨וּר׀וַיָּז֣וּבוּ מַיִם֮ וּנְחָלִ֪ים יִ֫שְׁטֹ֥פוּ הֲגַם־לֶ֭חֶם י֣וּכַל תֵּ֑ת אִם־יָכִ֖ין שְׁאֵ֣ר לְעַמּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Look, he struck a rock and flowed out waters and torrents overflowed; also bread is he able to give, or will he provide meat for his people?

en.L: Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck a rock and waters flowed out and torrents overflowed. \q Can {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} also give bread, \q or will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} provide meat for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people?"
en.B: Yes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hit the rock and water burst out and torrents swept along; \q but is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} able to give bread too, \q or to put meat before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people?"
en.R: Sure, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} hit a rock and water came gushing out in streams. \q But can {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} give bread too? \q Can {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} get meat for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people?"

decisions.choice: look ... can he also: a doubting question
decisions.reason: The people grant that God gave water, but doubt that he can do more. The question mocks rather than asks.

decisions.choice: bread and meat: manna and quail
decisions.reason: God answered the complaint with manna and quail (Exodus 16:12-13; Numbers 11:31), as verses 24-29 tell.

decisions.choice: meat: flesh to eat
decisions.reason: The word (she'er) is meat, as in verse 27.

source.text: לָכֵ֤ן׀שָׁמַ֥ע יְהוָ֗ה וַֽיִּתְעַבָּ֥ר וְ֭אֵשׁ נִשְּׂקָ֣ה בְיַעֲקֹ֑ב וְגַם־אַ֝֗ף עָלָ֥ה בְיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Therefore heard YHWH and was furious, and fire was kindled against Jacob, and also anger went up against Israel,

en.L: Therefore {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard and was furious; \q and a fire was kindled against Jacob, \q and anger also went up against Israel,
en.B: So when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard it, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was enraged; \q fire blazed up against Jacob, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger rose against Israel,
en.R: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} heard this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was very angry. \q Fire broke out among the people of Israel, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger flared up against them.

decisions.choice: fire was kindled: the fire at Taberah
decisions.reason: When the people complained, the LORD's fire burned among them at Taberah (Numbers 11:1-3); his anger burned again when they craved meat (Numbers 11:10, 33).

decisions.choice: anger went up: anger rising like smoke
decisions.reason: The word for anger ('af) is also "nose"; anger is pictured as hot breath or smoke rising (18:9).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 22 gives the reason ("because they did not believe"), so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

decisions.choice: the people of Israel; them
decisions.reason: Jacob and Israel name the same people; Readable says it once.

source.text: כִּ֤י לֹ֣א הֶ֭אֱמִינוּ בֵּאלֹהִ֑ים וְלֹ֥א בָ֝טְח֗וּ בִּֽישׁוּעָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: because not they believed in God, and not they trusted in his salvation.

en.L: because they did not believe in God \q and did not trust in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} salvation.
en.B: because they had no faith in God \q and did not rely on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power to save.
en.R: They did not believe God, \q and they did not trust {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to save them.

decisions.choice: they did not believe: the wilderness unbelief
decisions.reason: The LORD asked how long the people would not believe in him, after all the signs he had done (Numbers 14:11; Deuteronomy 1:32).

decisions.choice: salvation: rescue
decisions.reason: The word (yeshu'ah) is God's rescuing help, here his power to bring them through the wilderness (Exodus 14:13; 15:2).

source.text: וַיְצַ֣ו שְׁחָקִ֣ים מִמָּ֑עַל וְדַלְתֵ֖י שָׁמַ֣יִם פָּתָֽח׃

records.literal_gloss: And he commanded [the] skies from above, and [the] doors of heaven he opened,

en.L: Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} commanded the skies above \q and opened the doors of heaven,
en.B: Even so, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave orders to the clouds above \q and threw open the doors of the sky,
en.R: Even so, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave orders to the clouds above. \q He opened the doors of the sky.

decisions.choice: yet he commanded: grace in spite of unbelief
decisions.reason: Though they did not trust him, God still fed them. The psalm sets his kindness against their faithlessness again and again (verse 38).

decisions.choice: the doors of heaven: the sky opened to send down food
decisions.reason: The sky is pictured as having doors or windows that God opens to send rain or blessing (Genesis 7:11). Here they open to rain down bread.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verse 24, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: וַיַּמְטֵ֬ר עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם מָ֣ן לֶאֱכֹ֑ל וּדְגַן־שָׁ֝מַ֗יִם נָ֣תַן לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: and he rained down on them manna to eat, and [the] grain of heaven he gave to them.

en.L: and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rained down manna on them to eat, \q and gave them the grain of heaven.
en.B: and showered manna on them for food; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} handed them grain from heaven.
en.R: He made manna fall on them like rain so they could eat. \q It was grain from heaven.

decisions.choice: manna: bread from heaven
decisions.reason: God promised to "rain bread from heaven" and gave manna each morning (Exodus 16:4, 14-15, 31).

decisions.choice: quoted in John 6:31
decisions.reason: After Jesus fed the crowd, the people quoted this verse with Exodus 16: "He gave them bread from heaven to eat." Jesus answered that his Father gives the true bread from heaven, and that he is the bread of life (John 6:31-35).

decisions.choice: grain of heaven: food from God
decisions.reason: Manna is called grain because it was their bread; "of heaven" because it came from God, not from the ground.

source.text: לֶ֣חֶם אַ֭בִּירִים אָ֣כַל אִ֑ישׁ צֵידָ֬ה שָׁלַ֖ח לָהֶ֣ם לָשֹֽׂבַע׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] bread of mighty [ones] ate each one; provision he sent to them to fullness.

en.L: Each one ate the bread of the mighty; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them provision to the full.
en.B: Everyone ate the bread of the mighty ones; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent them supplies until they had their fill.
en.R: Each of them ate the food of angels. \q He sent them all they wanted to eat.

decisions.choice: the bread of the mighty: food from heaven's mighty ones
alternatives: the bread of angels (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The word ('abbirim) means mighty ones. Since the manna came from heaven, the mighty ones are taken as heaven's beings, the angels (103:20), as the ancient Greek translation says. It may simply mean food fit for nobles.

decisions.choice: each one: every person
decisions.reason: The word ('ish) here means each one of the people: no one went without (Exodus 16:16-18).

decisions.choice: angels
decisions.reason: Readable follows the likeliest sense (m1).

source.text: יַסַּ֣ע קָ֭דִים בַּשָּׁמָ֑יִם וַיְנַהֵ֖ג בְּעֻזּ֣וֹ תֵימָֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: He made set out an east wind in the heavens, and he drove by his strength a south wind.

en.L: He made an east wind set out in the heavens, \q and by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drove the south wind.
en.B: He set the east wind moving across the sky \q and steered the south wind by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power.
en.R: He made the east wind blow across the sky. \q With {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} sent the south wind too.

decisions.choice: the wind that brought the quail
decisions.reason: A wind went out from the LORD and brought quail from the sea (Numbers 11:31).

decisions.choice: set out, drove: God moves the winds like a herd
decisions.reason: The verbs (nasa', nahag) are used of breaking camp and driving a flock. God moves the winds as he moved his people (verse 52, "he drove them like a flock").

source.text: וַיַּמְטֵ֬ר עֲלֵיהֶ֣ם כֶּעָפָ֣ר שְׁאֵ֑ר וּֽכְח֥וֹל יַ֝מִּ֗ים ע֣וֹף כָּנָֽף׃

records.literal_gloss: And he rained on them like the dust meat, and like [the] sand of [the] seas birds of wing.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rained meat on them like dust, \q and winged birds like the sand of the seas.
en.B: He showered meat on them as thick as dust, \q birds on the wing as many as the grains of sand by the sea.
en.R: He made meat fall on them like rain, as thick as dust. \q He sent so many birds that they were like the sand on the seashore.

decisions.choice: meat and birds: the quail
decisions.reason: God sent quail into the camp in the evening (Exodus 16:13) and again in huge numbers at Kibroth-hattaavah (Numbers 11:31-32).

decisions.choice: like dust, like the sand of the seas: countless
decisions.reason: Dust and sand are pictures of what cannot be counted (Genesis 13:16; 22:17).

decisions.choice: made meat fall on them like rain
decisions.reason: Readable keeps the picture as a comparison.

source.text: וַ֭יַּפֵּל בְּקֶ֣רֶב מַחֲנֵ֑הוּ סָ֝בִ֗יב לְמִשְׁכְּנֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made fall in [the] midst of his camp, around his dwellings.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made [them] fall in the midst of his camp, \q all around his dwellings.
en.B: He brought them down in the middle of their camp, \q all around their tents.
en.R: The birds fell right in the middle of the camp, \q all around the tents where the people lived.

decisions.choice: his camp, his dwellings: Israel's camp
decisions.reason: The singular "his" refers to the people as one body, Israel (or Jacob, verse 21). Numbers 11:31 says the quail fell all around the camp.

decisions.choice: their (B); the people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "their" for the people (m1); Literal keeps the singular.

source.text: וַיֹּאכְל֣וּ וַיִּשְׂבְּע֣וּ מְאֹ֑ד וְ֝תַֽאֲוָתָ֗ם יָבִ֥א לָהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they ate and were satisfied exceedingly, and their desire he brought to them.

en.L: And they ate and were filled exceedingly, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them their desire.
en.B: They ate and were more than satisfied; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave them what they longed for.
en.R: They ate until they were stuffed. \q He gave them exactly what they wanted.

decisions.choice: their desire: their craving
decisions.reason: The word (ta'avah) is strong desire or craving. The place where the people died after the quail was named Kibroth-hattaavah, "graves of craving" (Numbers 11:34).

source.text: לֹא־זָר֥וּ מִתַּאֲוָתָ֑ם ע֝֗וֹד אָכְלָ֥ם בְּפִיהֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Not they had turned from their desire; still their food [was] in their mouth,

en.L: They had not turned from their craving; \q their food [was] still in their mouths,
en.B: They had not yet turned away from their craving; \q they were still chewing their food,
en.R: But they were still greedy for more. \q They were still chewing the food.

decisions.choice: they had not turned from their craving: they still craved
decisions.reason: Even with all they wanted, their craving had not left them. Numbers 11:33 says the meat was still between their teeth when the LORD struck them.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verse 31, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: וְאַ֤ף אֱלֹהִ֨ים׀עָ֘לָ֤ה בָהֶ֗ם וַֽ֭יַּהֲרֹג בְּמִשְׁמַנֵּיהֶ֑ם וּבַחוּרֵ֖י יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל הִכְרִֽיעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: and [the] anger of God went up against them, and he killed among their fat [ones], and [the] young men of Israel he struck down.

en.L: and the anger of God went up against them, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} killed some of their stoutest, \q and struck down the young men of Israel.
en.B: when the anger of God blazed against them; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} slew the best-fed among them \q and brought down the young men of Israel.
en.R: Then God became angry with them. \q He killed the strongest of them \q and cut down Israel's young men.

decisions.choice: he killed: the plague at Kibroth-hattaavah
decisions.reason: The LORD struck the people with a severe plague, and those who had craved were buried there (Numbers 11:33-34).

decisions.choice: their fat ones: the strongest and best-fed
decisions.reason: The word (mishmannim) is "fat ones", that is, the sturdy and well-fed, the men in their prime, parallel to "the young men".

source.text: בְּכָל־זֹ֭את חָֽטְאוּ־ע֑וֹד וְלֹֽא־הֶ֝אֱמִ֗ינוּ בְּנִפְלְאוֹתָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: In all this they sinned still, and not they believed in his wonders.

en.L: For all this they sinned still, \q and did not believe in {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders.
en.B: Even so they went on sinning; \q in spite of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} marvels they would not believe.
en.R: But even after all this, the people kept on sinning. \q Even after seeing {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} miracles, they still did not trust {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: they did not believe: the refusal to enter the land
decisions.reason: At Kadesh the people refused to go into the land; the LORD asked how long they would not believe in him in spite of all his signs (Numbers 14:11, 22-23).

decisions.choice: believe in his wonders: trust because of them
decisions.reason: The wonders should have led them to trust God; even they did not.

decisions.choice: the people; trust him
decisions.reason: Readable names who sinned and says whom they did not trust.

source.text: וַיְכַל־בַּהֶ֥בֶל יְמֵיהֶ֑ם וּ֝שְׁנוֹתָ֗ם בַּבֶּהָלָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he finished in the breath their days, and their years in the sudden terror.

en.L: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought their days to an end in a breath, \q and their years in sudden terror.
en.B: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let their days drift away like vapor \q and ended their years in sudden dread.
en.R: So {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} let their lives slip away for nothing. \q Their years ended in sudden terror.

decisions.choice: their days ended: the wilderness generation
decisions.reason: Because of their unbelief, that whole generation died in the wilderness during the forty years (Numbers 14:29-35).

decisions.choice: breath: what is fleeting and empty
decisions.reason: The word (hevel) is breath or vapor: what passes quickly and leaves nothing (39:6; Ecclesiastes 1:2). Their lives ran out with nothing to show for them.

source.text: אִם־הֲרָגָ֥ם וּדְרָשׁ֑וּהוּ וְ֝שָׁ֗בוּ וְשִֽׁחֲרוּ־אֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: When he killed them, then they sought him, and turned and sought earnestly God.

en.L: When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} killed them, they sought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q they turned back and sought God eagerly.
en.B: Whenever {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck them down, they would look for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q they would turn back and search hard for God.
en.R: Each time {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} killed some of them, the rest would turn to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q They would come back and look hard for God.

decisions.choice: when ... they sought: a repeated pattern
decisions.reason: The verb forms describe what happened again and again: punishment, then a turn back to God, then a relapse (verses 34-41).

decisions.choice: turned and sought earnestly: repented, eagerly
decisions.reason: "Turned" (shuv) is the word for repentance; the second verb (shichar) means to seek eagerly, perhaps at first light (63:2).

source.text: וַֽ֭יִּזְכְּרוּ כִּֽי־אֱלֹהִ֣ים צוּרָ֑ם וְאֵ֥ל עֶ֝לְיוֹן גֹּאֲלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And they remembered that God [was] their rock, and God Most High their redeemer.

en.L: And they remembered that God [was] their rock, \q and God Most High their redeemer.
en.B: They recalled that their Rock was God, \q that God Most High was the one who had set them free.
en.R: They remembered that God was like a strong rock that kept them safe. \q The God who is above all had rescued them.

decisions.choice: their rock: the song of Moses
decisions.reason: The song of Moses calls God the Rock and blames Israel for scorning the Rock of their salvation (Deuteronomy 32:4, 15).

decisions.choice: redeemer: the one who buys back and rescues
decisions.reason: The redeemer (go'el) is the near relative who buys back what was lost. God redeemed Israel from Egypt (Exodus 6:6; 15:13; 77:16).

decisions.choice: like a strong rock; the God who is above all
decisions.reason: Readable makes the picture a comparison and says what "Most High" means.

source.text: וַיְפַתּ֥וּהוּ בְּפִיהֶ֑ם וּ֝בִלְשׁוֹנָ֗ם יְכַזְּבוּ־לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: But they deceived him with their mouth, and with their tongue they lied to him,

en.L: But they deceived {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with their mouth, \q and with their tongue they lied to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
en.B: But their words to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} were only flattery; \q with their tongues they lied to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}},
en.R: But they were only pretending. \q Everything they said to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} was a lie.

decisions.choice: deceived: flattered, tried to win over
decisions.reason: The verb (patah) means to coax or deceive. Their turning back was talk only.

decisions.choice: mouth and tongue, not heart
decisions.reason: Isaiah 29:13 says the same of a people who honor God with their lips while their hearts are far from him.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 37 continues the thought ("their heart was not firm"), so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: וְ֭לִבָּם לֹא־נָכ֣וֹן עִמּ֑וֹ וְלֹ֥א נֶ֝אֶמְנ֗וּ בִּבְרִיתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: and their heart not [was] firm with him, and not they were faithful in his covenant.

en.L: and their heart was not firm toward {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, \q and they were not faithful to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant.
en.B: and their hearts were not set on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q they did not stay true to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant.
en.R: In their hearts they were not loyal to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q They did not keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} covenant.

decisions.choice: not firm, not faithful: as verse 8 warned
decisions.reason: The same two words describe the generation the children must not copy (verse 8): a heart not made firm and a spirit not faithful.

decisions.choice: faithful: firm, to be relied on
decisions.reason: The verb ('aman) is the root of "believe" in verses 22 and 32: they did not trust God and could not be trusted themselves.

source.text: וְה֤וּא רַח֨וּם׀יְכַפֵּ֥ר עָוֺן֮ וְֽלֹא־יַ֫שְׁחִ֥ית וְ֭הִרְבָּה לְהָשִׁ֣יב אַפּ֑וֹ וְלֹֽא־יָ֝עִיר כָּל־חֲמָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: But he, compassionate, atones for iniquity and does not destroy, and often he turned back his anger and did not stir up all his rage.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, being compassionate, atoned for iniquity and did not destroy [them]; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} often turned back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger \q and did not stir up all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} rage.
en.B: Yet {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was full of compassion; {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} covered their guilt and did not wipe them out. \q Many a time {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} held back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger \q and did not let all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fury loose.
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was kind and full of mercy. He forgave their sins and did not wipe them out. \q Many times {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} held back {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger \q and did not let all of it pour out.

decisions.choice: compassionate: God's own description
decisions.reason: God described himself to Moses as compassionate and gracious, slow to anger (Exodus 34:6-7). At Moses' prayer he forgave the people in the wilderness (Numbers 14:18-20).

decisions.choice: atones for: covers over guilt
decisions.reason: The verb (kipper) means to cover or wipe away guilt so that it no longer stands between God and his people (65:4; 79:9).

decisions.choice: atones, does not destroy: what he always does
decisions.reason: The verbs describe God's habit: again and again he forgave instead of destroying.

source.text: וַ֭יִּזְכֹּר כִּי־בָשָׂ֣ר הֵ֑מָּה ר֥וּחַ ה֝וֹלֵ֗ךְ וְלֹ֣א יָשֽׁוּב׃

records.literal_gloss: And he remembered that flesh [were] they, a wind [that] goes and not returns.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} remembered that they [were] flesh, \q a wind that passes and does not return.
en.B: He remembered that they were only flesh, \q a breeze that blows past and does not come back.
en.R: He remembered that they were only human. \q Their life is like a breath of wind that blows by and is gone.

decisions.choice: flesh: frail mortals
decisions.reason: Flesh (basar) is human life in its weakness (Genesis 6:3; 56:5). God remembers how frail people are (103:14).

decisions.choice: a wind that goes and does not return: life that passes
decisions.reason: A breath of wind passes and is gone; so is a human life (Job 7:7). God's mercy takes account of how short it is.

decisions.choice: only flesh (B); only human (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced adds "only" to bring out the point; Readable says what "flesh" means (m1).

source.text: כַּ֭מָּה יַמְר֣וּהוּ בַמִּדְבָּ֑ר יַ֝עֲצִיב֗וּהוּ בִּֽישִׁימֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: How often they rebelled against him in the wilderness, grieved him in [the] wasteland!

en.L: How often they rebelled against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the wilderness, \q [and] grieved {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the wasteland!
en.B: How many times they defied {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the wilderness \q and caused {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} grief in the barren land!
en.R: Again and again they turned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in the desert. \q They gave {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} pain in that empty land.

decisions.choice: how often: ten times
decisions.reason: The LORD said the wilderness generation had tested him "these ten times" (Numbers 14:22).

decisions.choice: grieved him: caused him pain
decisions.reason: The verb ('atsav) means to hurt or cause sorrow. Isaiah 63 says the same of Israel in the wilderness, who grieved God's Holy Spirit.

source.text: וַיָּשׁ֣וּבוּ וַיְנַסּ֣וּ אֵ֑ל וּקְד֖וֹשׁ יִשְׂרָאֵ֣ל הִתְווּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they turned and tested God, and [the] Holy One of Israel they pained.

en.L: And they again tested God, \q and pained the Holy One of Israel.
en.B: Once more they challenged God \q and wounded the Holy One of Israel.
en.R: Over and over they tested God's patience. \q They caused pain to the Holy One of Israel.

decisions.choice: they turned and tested: they tested again
decisions.reason: "Turned" (shuv) before another verb means doing it again. The word that meant repentance in verse 34 now means relapse.

decisions.choice: pained: hurt, provoked
decisions.reason: The verb (hitwu) occurs only here in this form. It is taken as "pained" or "provoked"; older translations read "limited" or "set a mark for".

decisions.choice: the Holy One of Israel: a title of God
decisions.reason: The title names God as holy and as bound to Israel; it is frequent in Isaiah (Isaiah 1:4) and appears in 71:22 and 89:19.

source.text: לֹא־זָכְר֥וּ אֶת־יָד֑וֹ י֝֗וֹם אֲֽשֶׁר־פָּדָ֥ם מִנִּי־צָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Not they remembered his hand, [the] day when he ransomed them from [the] foe,

en.L: They did not remember {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand, \q the day when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} ransomed them from the foe,
en.B: They forgot {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power \q and the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} bought them free from the enemy,
en.R: They forgot how powerful {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was \q on the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rescued them from their enemies.

decisions.choice: his hand: his power at work
decisions.reason: God brought Israel out of Egypt "with a strong hand" (Exodus 13:9; Deuteronomy 7:8).

decisions.choice: ransomed: set free at a cost
decisions.reason: The verb (padah) means to free by paying a price; God ransomed Israel from slavery (Deuteronomy 7:8; 13:6).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 43 tells what that day was, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: אֲשֶׁר־שָׂ֣ם בְּ֭מִצְרַיִם אֹֽתוֹתָ֑יו וּ֝מוֹפְתָ֗יו בִּשְׂדֵה־צֹֽעַן׃

records.literal_gloss: when he set in Egypt his signs, and his wonders in [the] field of Zoan.

en.L: when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} set {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} signs in Egypt, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonders in the field of Zoan.
en.B: when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} displayed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} signs in Egypt \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} marvels in the fields around Zoan.
en.R: That was when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did miracles and amazing things in Egypt, \q around the city of Zoan.

decisions.choice: signs and wonders: the plagues of Egypt
decisions.reason: God set his signs in Egypt so that Israel would tell them to their children (Exodus 10:1-2; Deuteronomy 4:34). Verses 44-51 list them.

decisions.choice: seven plagues, in a different order
decisions.reason: The psalm names seven of the plagues of Exodus 7-12, not in the order Exodus gives them, and ends as Exodus does with the death of the firstborn. It is a poem recalling the events, not a list.

decisions.choice: That was
decisions.reason: Readable begins a new sentence, so it links it to verse 42.

source.text: וַיַּהֲפֹ֣ךְ לְ֭דָם יְאֹרֵיהֶ֑ם וְ֝נֹזְלֵיהֶ֗ם בַּל־יִשְׁתָּיֽוּן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he turned to blood their channels, and their streams not they could drink.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned their Nile channels into blood, \q and their streams [so that] they could not drink.
en.B: He changed their rivers into blood, \q and their running water could not be drunk.
en.R: He turned their rivers into blood, \q so the Egyptians had no water to drink.

decisions.choice: turned to blood: the first plague
decisions.reason: Moses struck the Nile and its water became blood, so the Egyptians could not drink it (Exodus 7:17-21).

decisions.choice: channels: the Nile and its branches
decisions.reason: The word (ye'orim) is the plural of the word for the Nile: the river, its arms and its canals (Exodus 7:19).

decisions.choice: the Egyptians
decisions.reason: Readable names who "they" are; the psalm moves straight into the plagues on Egypt.

source.text: יְשַׁלַּ֬ח בָּהֶ֣ם עָ֭רֹב וַיֹּאכְלֵ֑ם וּ֝צְפַרְדֵּ֗עַ וַתַּשְׁחִיתֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: He sent among them swarm[s] and it devoured them, and frog[s] and it ruined them.

en.L: He sent swarms among them, and they devoured them, \q and frogs, and they ruined them.
en.B: He sent swarms of insects among them to eat them up, \q and frogs to bring them to ruin.
en.R: He sent swarms of flies to bite them \q and frogs to ruin their land.

decisions.choice: swarms and frogs: plagues of Exodus 8
decisions.reason: The frogs came up over the land and the swarms filled the houses of Egypt (Exodus 8).

decisions.choice: swarm: biting insects
decisions.reason: The word ('arov) names a swarm, traditionally of flies; Exodus 8 says the land was ruined by them.

decisions.choice: to bite them; to ruin their land
decisions.reason: Readable says how the swarms and frogs harmed them.

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לֶחָסִ֣יל יְבוּלָ֑ם וִֽ֝יגִיעָ֗ם לָאַרְבֶּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gave to the locust their produce, and their toil to the locust.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave their produce to the grasshopper, \q and their toil to the locust.
en.B: He handed their harvest over to the grasshopper \q and all they had worked for to the swarming locust.
en.R: He let locusts eat up their crops \q and everything they had worked to grow.

decisions.choice: the locusts: the eighth plague
decisions.reason: Locusts covered the land and ate every plant the hail had left (Exodus 10:12-15).

decisions.choice: two words for locust
decisions.reason: The first word (chasil) is a kind of locust, perhaps a stage of it (1 Kings 8:37); the second ('arbeh) is the usual word, used in Exodus 10.

source.text: יַהֲרֹ֣ג בַּבָּרָ֣ד גַּפְנָ֑ם וְ֝שִׁקְמוֹתָ֗ם בַּֽחֲנָמַֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: He killed with the hail their vine[s], and their sycamore figs with frost.

en.L: He killed their vines with hail, \q and their sycamore figs with frost.
en.B: He struck their vines dead with hail \q and froze their sycamore-figs with ice.
en.R: He ruined their grapevines with hail \q and their fig trees with ice.

decisions.choice: hail: the seventh plague
decisions.reason: Hail struck everything in the fields of Egypt and broke every tree (Exodus 9:22-25).

decisions.choice: frost: a word whose sense is not certain
decisions.reason: The word (chanamal) occurs only here. It is taken as frost or ice, in parallel with hail.

decisions.choice: sycamore figs: a fig tree of Egypt
decisions.reason: The sycamore fig grew widely in Egypt and the lowlands, giving fruit and timber (1 Kings 10:27).

source.text: וַיַּסְגֵּ֣ר לַבָּרָ֣ד בְּעִירָ֑ם וּ֝מִקְנֵיהֶ֗ם לָרְשָׁפִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gave over to the hail their cattle, and their livestock to the flames.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave over their cattle to the hail, \q and their livestock to bolts of fire.
en.B: He left their cattle at the mercy of the hail, \q and their herds to the flashing fire.
en.R: He let hail kill their cattle \q and lightning strike their herds.

decisions.choice: cattle given to the hail
decisions.reason: The hail killed the animals left in the fields, and fire ran down to the ground with it (Exodus 9:19-25).

decisions.choice: flames: bolts of lightning
decisions.reason: The word (reshafim) means flames, here lightning (76:4). It can also mean plague (Deuteronomy 32:24), and the line may recall the plague on Egypt's livestock (Exodus 9:3-6).

source.text: יְשַׁלַּח־בָּ֨ם׀חֲר֬וֹן אַפּ֗וֹ עֶבְרָ֣ה וָזַ֣עַם וְצָרָ֑ה מִ֝שְׁלַ֗חַת מַלְאֲכֵ֥י רָעִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: He sent against them [the] burning of his anger, fury and indignation and distress, a sending of messengers of harm.

en.L: He sent against them the burning of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger, \q fury and indignation and distress, \q a company of messengers of harm.
en.B: He let loose on them the heat of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger, \q rage and fury and distress, \q a troop of angels bringing disaster.
en.R: He let {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} burning anger loose on them, with all {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} fury and wrath. \q He sent a band of angels to bring disaster on them.

decisions.choice: messengers of harm: angels sent to bring disaster
decisions.reason: The phrase means messengers (mal'akhim) who bring harm (ra'im), not angels who are evil. On the night of the firstborn the LORD's "destroyer" passed through Egypt (Exodus 12:23).

decisions.choice: a list of words for anger
decisions.reason: Four words for anger and its effects stand side by side: burning anger, fury, indignation and distress. Together they are what God "sent", like a troop of messengers.

source.text: יְפַלֵּ֥ס נָתִ֗יב לְאַ֫פּ֥וֹ לֹא־חָשַׂ֣ךְ מִמָּ֣וֶת נַפְשָׁ֑ם וְ֝חַיָּתָ֗ם לַדֶּ֥בֶר הִסְגִּֽיר׃

records.literal_gloss: He leveled a path for his anger; not he spared from death their soul, and their life to the pestilence he gave over.

en.L: He leveled a path for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not spare their soul from death, \q but gave their life over to the plague.
en.B: He cleared a road for {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} did not hold them back from death, \q but handed their lives over to the plague.
en.R: He let {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger have its way. \q He did not save them from death. \q He let the plague take their lives.

decisions.choice: leveled a path for his anger: gave it free course
decisions.reason: A leveled road lets traffic run without hindrance; God let his anger run on without holding it back, as he had held it back from Israel (verse 38).

decisions.choice: their life: the Egyptians, or their animals
decisions.reason: The word (chayyatam) is "their life", parallel to "their soul". The same word can mean living creatures, so the line may mean the plague that killed Egypt's livestock (Exodus 9:3-6).

decisions.choice: them
decisions.reason: As in Psalms 1-12, nefesh is "soul" at Literal and the person at Balanced and Readable.

source.text: וַיַּ֣ךְ כָּל־בְּכ֣וֹר בְּמִצְרָ֑יִם רֵאשִׁ֥ית א֝וֹנִ֗ים בְּאָהֳלֵי־חָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he struck every firstborn in Egypt, [the] first of strength in [the] tents of Ham.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck every firstborn in Egypt, \q the first of [their] strength in the tents of Ham.
en.B: He cut down every firstborn in Egypt, \q the eldest sons, the first of their strength, throughout the tents of Ham.
en.R: He killed every firstborn in Egypt, \q the oldest son in each family of Ham's descendants.

decisions.choice: every firstborn: the last plague
decisions.reason: At midnight the LORD struck every firstborn in Egypt, from Pharaoh's son to the firstborn of the animals (Exodus 12:29).

decisions.choice: the first of strength: the firstborn son
decisions.reason: Jacob calls Reuben "the first of my strength" (Genesis 49:3; Deuteronomy 21:17): the firstborn is the first sign of a father's vigor.

decisions.choice: the tents of Ham: Egypt
decisions.reason: Egypt (Mizraim) was a son of Ham (Genesis 10:6), so Egypt is called the land of Ham (105:23; 106:22).

decisions.choice: the oldest son in each family of Ham's descendants
alternatives: the first of strength in the tents of Ham
decisions.reason: Readable says what the two pictures mean (m2, m3).

source.text: וַיַּסַּ֣ע כַּצֹּ֣אן עַמּ֑וֹ וַֽיְנַהֲגֵ֥ם כַּ֝עֵ֗דֶר בַּמִּדְבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he made set out like the sheep his people, and he drove them like the flock in the wilderness.

en.L: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led out {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people like sheep, \q and drove them like a flock in the wilderness.
en.B: Then {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} moved {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people out like sheep \q and herded them like a flock across the wilderness.
en.R: But {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own people out like a shepherd leading sheep. \q He guided them through the desert like a flock.

decisions.choice: he led out his people like sheep: the exodus
decisions.reason: Israel set out from Egypt (Exodus 12:37) with God as their shepherd, as 77:21 also says. The verb (nasa') is the one used of the wind in verse 26.

decisions.choice: God as shepherd, Egypt struck
decisions.reason: The same God who struck Egypt's firstborn (verse 51) cares for Israel as a shepherd cares for his sheep. The picture prepares for David the shepherd (verses 70-72).

source.text: וַיַּנְחֵ֣ם לָ֭בֶטַח וְלֹ֣א פָחָ֑דוּ וְאֶת־א֝וֹיְבֵיהֶ֗ם כִּסָּ֥ה הַיָּֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he guided them to safety, and not they feared, and their enemies covered the sea.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} guided them in safety, and they did not fear; \q but the sea covered their enemies.
en.B: He kept them safe as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} led them, and they were not afraid; \q but the sea closed over their enemies.
en.R: He kept them safe, so they were not afraid. \q But the sea covered their enemies and drowned them.

decisions.choice: the sea covered their enemies
decisions.reason: Moses told the people not to fear (Exodus 14:13); the waters returned and covered Pharaoh's army (Exodus 14:28; 15:10).

decisions.choice: and drowned them
decisions.reason: Readable makes plain what being covered by the sea meant.

source.text: וַ֭יְבִיאֵם אֶל־גְּב֣וּל קָדְשׁ֑וֹ הַר־זֶ֝֗ה קָנְתָ֥ה יְמִינֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he brought them to [the] territory of his holiness, [the] mountain [which] this acquired his right hand.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought them to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy territory, \q this mountain [that] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} right hand acquired.
en.B: He led them to {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sacred land, \q to these mountains that {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own power had gained.
en.R: He brought them into {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} holy land, \q to the hills {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had won for them by {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power.

decisions.choice: the mountain his right hand acquired: the song at the sea
decisions.reason: The song of Moses says God would bring his people in and plant them on the mountain of his inheritance, the sanctuary his hands established (Exodus 15:16-17).

decisions.choice: this mountain: the hill country of the land
decisions.reason: The mountain may be the hill country of Canaan as a whole (Deuteronomy 3:25) or Mount Zion, where the story ends (verse 68).

decisions.choice: territory: land within borders
decisions.reason: The word (gevul) is a border and the land it encloses.

source.text: וַיְגָ֤רֶשׁ מִפְּנֵיהֶ֨ם׀גּוֹיִ֗ם וַֽ֭יַּפִּילֵם בְּחֶ֣בֶל נַחֲלָ֑ה וַיַּשְׁכֵּ֥ן בְּ֝אָהֳלֵיהֶ֗ם שִׁבְטֵ֥י יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: And he drove out from before them nations, and he allotted them by [the] line [as] an inheritance, and he made dwell in their tents [the] tribes of Israel.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} drove out nations before them, \q and allotted them by measuring line [as] an inheritance, \q and made the tribes of Israel dwell in their tents.
en.B: He pushed out nations ahead of them \q and shared out their land by measuring line as a possession; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave the tribes of Israel their tents to live in.
en.R: He forced the nations out of the land ahead of them. \q He divided the land among the tribes of Israel and gave them homes there.

decisions.choice: he drove out nations: the conquest
decisions.reason: God drove out the nations of Canaan before Israel (Joshua 24:12, 18), and the land was divided among the tribes (Joshua 13-21).

decisions.choice: allotted them; their tents
alternatives: he allotted the tribes their inheritance
decisions.reason: "Them" is taken as the nations' land, measured out for Israel, and "their tents" as the nations' former homes now given to Israel (Deuteronomy 6:10-11).

decisions.choice: line: a measuring cord
decisions.reason: Land was measured out with a cord (chevel), so the word came to mean an allotted share (16:6; 105:11).

source.text: וַיְנַסּ֣וּ וַ֭יַּמְרוּ אֶת־אֱלֹהִ֣ים עֶלְי֑וֹן וְ֝עֵדוֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א שָׁמָֽרוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they tested and rebelled against God Most High, and his testimonies not they kept.

en.L: But they tested and rebelled against God Most High, \q and did not keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} testimonies.
en.B: Still they challenged God Most High and defied {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}; \q they did not keep {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} decrees.
en.R: But the people still tested the God who is above all and turned against {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. \q They did not obey {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} laws.

decisions.choice: they tested and rebelled: the time of the judges
decisions.reason: In the land the next generation did not know the LORD and served other gods (Judges 2:10-13). The wilderness story repeats itself (verses 17-18, 40-41).

decisions.choice: testimonies: God's decrees
decisions.reason: The plural of the word in verse 5 ('edot): the terms of God's covenant.

source.text: וַיִּסֹּ֣גוּ וַֽ֭יִּבְגְּדוּ כַּאֲבוֹתָ֑ם נֶ֝הְפְּכ֗וּ כְּקֶ֣שֶׁת רְמִיָּֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And they turned back and were treacherous like their fathers; they turned like a bow of deceit.

en.L: And they turned back and acted treacherously like their fathers; \q they twisted like a deceitful bow.
en.B: They turned away and broke faith as their ancestors did; \q they went crooked like a warped bow.
en.R: Like their ancestors, they turned away from God and could not be trusted. \q They were like a bent bow that misses its target.

decisions.choice: a deceitful bow: a bow that cannot be relied on
decisions.reason: A bow that is warped or slack sends the arrow wide. Hosea 7 uses the same picture for Israel. It recalls the archers of Ephraim who turned back (verse 9).

decisions.choice: were treacherous: broke faith
decisions.reason: The verb (bagad) is used for unfaithfulness in a bond, such as marriage or covenant.

decisions.choice: from God
decisions.reason: Readable names whom they turned away from.

source.text: וַיַּכְעִיס֥וּהוּ בְּבָמוֹתָ֑ם וּ֝בִפְסִילֵיהֶ֗ם יַקְנִיאֽוּהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And they provoked him to anger with their high places, and with their idols they made him jealous.

en.L: And they provoked {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} to anger with their high places, \q and with their carved images they made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} jealous.
en.B: They angered {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} with their hilltop shrines, \q and by their idols roused {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} jealous anger.
en.R: They made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} angry by worshiping at shrines on the hills. \q Their idols made {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} jealous.

decisions.choice: high places: local hilltop shrines
decisions.reason: The high places (bamot) were shrines on hills and raised platforms, where Israel often worshiped other gods or the LORD in forbidden ways (1 Kings 3:2; 14:23).

decisions.choice: anger and jealousy: the song of Moses
decisions.reason: The song of Moses says Israel made God jealous with foreign gods and angry with idols (Deuteronomy 32:16, 21). God's jealousy is the claim of covenant love that will not share his people with other gods (Exodus 20:5).

decisions.choice: idols: carved images
decisions.reason: The word (pesilim) means images carved from wood or stone (Deuteronomy 7:5).

source.text: שָׁמַ֣ע אֱ֭לֹהִים וַֽיִּתְעַבָּ֑ר וַיִּמְאַ֥ס מְ֝אֹ֗ד בְּיִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃

records.literal_gloss: Heard God and was furious, and he rejected exceedingly Israel.

en.L: God heard and was furious, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} utterly rejected Israel.
en.B: When God heard, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} anger blazed, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} cast Israel off entirely.
en.R: When God heard this, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was very angry, \q and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} turned completely away from Israel.

decisions.choice: heard and was furious: as in verse 21
decisions.reason: The words repeat verse 21. As then, God's anger answers his people's sin; this time it falls in the days of Eli at Shiloh (verses 60-64).

decisions.choice: rejected Israel: rejected the people as they then were
decisions.reason: The rejection is of Israel in the time of Shiloh; the psalm goes on to tell how God chose Judah, Zion and David (verses 67-70). It is not an end of his covenant (verse 38).

records.literal_gloss: And he abandoned [the] dwelling of Shiloh, [the] tent [where] he dwelt among humankind.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} abandoned the dwelling of Shiloh, \q the tent [where] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} dwelt among humankind.
en.B: He deserted the sanctuary at Shiloh, \q the tent where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} home among people.
en.R: He left the holy tent at Shiloh, \q where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} had lived among people.

decisions.choice: Shiloh: where the tabernacle stood
decisions.reason: The tabernacle was set up at Shiloh after the conquest (Joshua 18:1) and stood there through the days of the judges and of Eli and Samuel (1 Samuel 1-4). Jeremiah later points to Shiloh as the place God had abandoned (Jeremiah 7:12-14; 26:6).

decisions.choice: dwelling: the tabernacle
decisions.reason: The word (mishkan) is the tent-sanctuary where God dwelt among Israel (Exodus 25:8-9).

decisions.choice: sanctuary (B); holy tent (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what kind of dwelling is meant (m2).

source.text: וַיִּתֵּ֣ן לַשְּׁבִ֣י עֻזּ֑וֹ וְֽתִפְאַרְתּ֥וֹ בְיַד־צָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he gave to the captivity his strength, and his splendor into [the] hand of [the] foe.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} strength into captivity, \q and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} splendor into the hand of the foe.
en.B: He let {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} might be carried off as a captive, \q {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory into enemy hands.
en.R: He let the enemy capture the ark, \q the sign of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} power and glory.

decisions.choice: his strength and splendor: the ark of the covenant
decisions.reason: The ark, the sign of God's presence and power (132:8, "the ark of your strength"), was captured by the Philistines at the battle of Aphek. Eli's daughter-in-law named her son Ichabod, saying "the glory has gone from Israel" (1 Samuel 4:11, 21-22).

decisions.choice: the ark, the sign of his power and glory
decisions.reason: Readable names what the two words refer to (m1).

source.text: וַיַּסְגֵּ֣ר לַחֶ֣רֶב עַמּ֑וֹ וּ֝בְנַחֲלָת֗וֹ הִתְעַבָּֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he delivered up to the sword his people, and with his inheritance he was furious.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people over to the sword, \q and was furious with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance.
en.B: He handed {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people over to the sword; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} raged against {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own inheritance.
en.R: He let enemies kill {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people in battle. \q He was very angry with the people who belonged to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: his people given to the sword: the defeat at Aphek
decisions.reason: Thirty thousand Israelite soldiers fell in the battle in which the ark was taken (1 Samuel 4:10).

decisions.choice: his inheritance: his own people
decisions.reason: Israel is called God's inheritance (nachalah), the people who belong to him (Deuteronomy 9:29; 28:9). He was angry with his own.

source.text: בַּחוּרָ֥יו אָֽכְלָה־אֵ֑שׁ וּ֝בְתוּלֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א הוּלָּֽלוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: His young men fire consumed, and his young women not were praised.

en.L: Fire consumed his young men, \q and his young women were not praised [in a wedding song].
en.B: Their young men were eaten up by fire; \q no one sang the wedding song for their young women.
en.R: War burned up their young men \q like fire, so the young women had no one to marry.

decisions.choice: his young men: the people's
decisions.reason: "His" here and in verse 64 refers to the people ("his people", verse 62) as one body, not to God.

decisions.choice: not praised: no wedding song was sung for them
alternatives: were not mourned (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The verb (hullal) means "were praised", here with the songs sung at a wedding: with the young men dead, there were no weddings. The ancient Greek translation reads "were not mourned".

decisions.choice: fire consumed: the destruction of war
decisions.reason: Fire stands for the ruin of war (Numbers 21:28) and for God's anger (verse 21).

decisions.choice: their
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "their" for the people (m1).

source.text: כֹּ֭הֲנָיו בַּחֶ֣רֶב נָפָ֑לוּ וְ֝אַלְמְנֹתָ֗יו לֹ֣א תִבְכֶּֽינָה׃

records.literal_gloss: His priests by the sword fell, and his widows not wept.

en.L: His priests fell by the sword, \q and his widows did not weep.
en.B: Their priests were cut down by the sword, \q and the widows they left could not raise a lament.
en.R: Their priests were killed in battle, \q and their widows were not even able to mourn for them.

decisions.choice: priests fell: Hophni and Phinehas
decisions.reason: Eli's sons Hophni and Phinehas, priests at Shiloh, died in the battle (1 Samuel 4:11). The wife of Phinehas died giving birth when the news came (1 Samuel 4:19-20).

decisions.choice: did not weep: could not hold the mourning rites
decisions.reason: In such a disaster there was no time or place for the usual laments for the dead (Job 27:15).

decisions.choice: their
decisions.reason: As in verse 63, "his" refers to the people.

source.text: וַיִּקַ֖ץ כְּיָשֵׁ֥ן׀אֲדֹנָ֑י כְּ֝גִבּ֗וֹר מִתְרוֹנֵ֥ן מִיָּֽיִן׃

records.literal_gloss: And awoke as one sleeping [the] Lord, like a warrior shouting from wine.

en.L: Then [the] Lord awoke like one asleep, \q like a warrior shouting from wine.
en.B: Then the Lord roused {{deity_pronoun:himself|Himself}} like a sleeper waking, \q like a warrior shouting as the wine stirs him.
en.R: Then the Lord got up like someone waking from sleep. \q He was like a mighty soldier who has been drinking wine and shouts for battle.

decisions.choice: the Lord awoke: a bold picture
decisions.reason: God does not sleep (121:4), but when he seems to do nothing his people say he is asleep (44:24). The picture of him waking means that he now acts suddenly and with power.

decisions.choice: shouting: crying out
decisions.reason: The form (mitronen) is taken from the verb for a ringing shout: the warrior's battle cry when wine has given him courage. Some take it as "overcome" (by wine), from another root.

source.text: וַיַּךְ־צָרָ֥יו אָח֑וֹר חֶרְפַּ֥ת ע֝וֹלָ֗ם נָ֣תַן לָֽמוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And he struck his foes backward; a reproach of perpetuity he gave to them.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} struck {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} foes backward; \q {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} put on them an everlasting reproach.
en.B: He beat {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies back \q and put them to lasting shame.
en.R: He drove {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} enemies back \q and disgraced them forever.

decisions.choice: he struck his foes: the Philistines
decisions.reason: While the ark was among them, the LORD struck the Philistines with tumors until they sent it back (1 Samuel 5-6); later David defeated them (2 Samuel 5).

decisions.choice: backward: driving them back
decisions.reason: The word ('achor) means back or behind: God drove his enemies back, or struck them from behind. Some have seen in it the tumors of 1 Samuel 5.

source.text: וַ֭יִּמְאַס בְּאֹ֣הֶל יוֹסֵ֑ף וּֽבְשֵׁ֥בֶט אֶ֝פְרַ֗יִם לֹ֣א בָחָֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And he rejected [the] tent of Joseph, and [the] tribe of Ephraim not he chose,

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} rejected the tent of Joseph, \q and did not choose the tribe of Ephraim,
en.B: He turned down the tent of Joseph; \q Ephraim's tribe was not the one {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose,
en.R: He turned away from the family of Joseph. \q He did not choose the tribe of Ephraim.

decisions.choice: the tent of Joseph, the tribe of Ephraim
decisions.reason: Joseph's sons Ephraim and Manasseh were the leading northern tribes; Shiloh lay in Ephraim's land (Joshua 18:1). God did not choose them for the sanctuary or the king.

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: Verse 68 completes the contrast ("but he chose the tribe of Judah"), so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: וַ֭יִּבְחַר אֶת־שֵׁ֣בֶט יְהוּדָ֑ה אֶֽת־הַ֥ר צִ֝יּ֗וֹן אֲשֶׁ֣ר אָהֵֽב׃

records.literal_gloss: but he chose the tribe of Judah, Mount Zion which he loved.

en.L: but {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose the tribe of Judah, \q Mount Zion, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved.
en.B: instead {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} picked out the tribe of Judah \q and Mount Zion, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} holds dear.
en.R: Instead {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose the tribe of Judah \q and Mount Zion, the place {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} loved.

decisions.choice: he chose Judah: the tribe of the king
decisions.reason: Jacob's blessing gave the scepter to Judah (Genesis 49:10), and David says God chose Judah as ruler (1 Chronicles 28:4).

decisions.choice: Mount Zion: the hill of the temple
decisions.reason: Zion was the stronghold David took (2 Samuel 5:7) and where the ark and later the temple stood. God "loves the gates of Zion" (87:2).

source.text: וַיִּ֣בֶן כְּמוֹ־רָ֭מִים מִקְדָּשׁ֑וֹ כְּ֝אֶ֗רֶץ יְסָדָ֥הּ לְעוֹלָֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he built like [the] heights his sanctuary, like [the] earth [which] he founded it forever.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} built {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sanctuary like the heights, \q like the earth [that] {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} founded forever.
en.B: He made {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} sanctuary as lofty as the heavens \q and as firm as the earth, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} founded to last forever.
en.R: He built {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} temple there. He made it tall like the sky \q and solid like the earth, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} made to last forever.

decisions.choice: the heights: the heavens
decisions.reason: The word (ramim) means high things, the heavens or the high places. The temple is compared to heaven above and to the earth below.

decisions.choice: his sanctuary: the temple in Jerusalem
decisions.reason: The temple was built on Zion by Solomon (1 Kings 6), and God chose Zion as his dwelling forever (132:13-14).

decisions.choice: as lofty as; as firm as
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say in what way the sanctuary is like the heights and the earth: high and lasting.

source.text: וַ֭יִּבְחַר בְּדָוִ֣ד עַבְדּ֑וֹ וַ֝יִּקָּחֵ֗הוּ מִֽמִּכְלְאֹ֥ת צֹֽאן׃

records.literal_gloss: And he chose David his servant, and took him from [the] folds of sheep.

en.L: And {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} chose David {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, \q and took him from the sheepfolds,
en.B: He singled out David, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant, \q and called him away from the sheepfolds,
en.R: He chose {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} servant David, \q who was looking after sheep in their pens.

decisions.choice: he chose David from the sheepfolds
decisions.reason: Samuel anointed David, the youngest son, who was out keeping the sheep (1 Samuel 16:11-13). God told David, "I took you from the pasture, from following the sheep" (2 Samuel 7:8).

decisions.choice: his servant: one God chose for his work
decisions.reason: "Servant" ('eved) is a title of honor for those God uses, such as Moses and David (18:1; 89:4).

decisions.choice: a sentence that runs on
decisions.reason: The sentence continues into verse 71, so this verse ends with a comma at Literal and Balanced.

source.text: מֵאַחַ֥ר עָל֗וֹת הֱ֫בִיא֥וֹ לִ֭רְעוֹת בְּיַעֲקֹ֣ב עַמּ֑וֹ וּ֝בְיִשְׂרָאֵ֗ל נַחֲלָתֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: from after nursing [ewes] he brought him to shepherd Jacob his people, and Israel his inheritance.

en.L: from following the nursing ewes {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought him \q to shepherd Jacob {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, \q and Israel {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} inheritance.
en.B: from walking behind the nursing ewes {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} brought him \q to care for Jacob, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} people, \q and for Israel, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} own possession, as their shepherd.
en.R: God took him away from the mother sheep and their lambs. \q He made him the shepherd of Israel, the people who belonged to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

decisions.choice: to shepherd: to rule as king
decisions.reason: A king was called the shepherd of his people. God told David, "You will shepherd my people Israel" (2 Samuel 5:2).

decisions.choice: nursing ewes: sheep with young lambs
decisions.reason: The word ('alot) is ewes giving suck, which a shepherd must lead gently (Genesis 33:13; Isaiah 40:11). David's care for them fitted him to care for God's people.

decisions.choice: God
decisions.reason: Readable starts a new sentence and names who acts.

source.text: וַ֭יִּרְעֵם כְּתֹ֣ם לְבָב֑וֹ וּבִתְבוּנ֖וֹת כַּפָּ֣יו יַנְחֵֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: And he shepherded them according to [the] integrity of his heart, and with [the] skill of his hands he led them.

en.L: And he shepherded them according to the integrity of his heart, \q and led them by the skill of his hands.
en.B: He cared for them as a shepherd with an honest heart \q and led them with skillful hands.
en.R: David took care of them with a good and honest heart. \q He led them wisely and well.

decisions.choice: he shepherded them: David
decisions.reason: "He" is David, the shepherd king of verses 70-71, so there is no capital or span for him. The long story ends with God's answer to Israel's unfaithfulness: a king after his own heart.

decisions.choice: integrity: wholeness of heart
decisions.reason: The word (tom) is completeness or honesty. God told Solomon to walk as David had walked, in integrity of heart (1 Kings 9:4).

decisions.choice: David
decisions.reason: Readable names who "he" is (m1).
